chapter: Cab Calloway, Harlem and New York musicians
title: Hugh Wiley's society gig with no intermission
summary: Danny played with Hugh Wiley, who sat at the piano from eight to twelve and refused any intermission.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: But he was well-loved with those people, and he played... And all ...(?)... that thing, they don't stop playing. The last one I did, the one I played with, that's where them other people got there -- them big-band leaders, society band leaders.
Yeah. They got that for real, boy.

Continuously. I played with Wiley(?), Hugh Wiley(?). Hugh Wiley. I played the last one with him. That's the first time I played one. And he got on the piano at eight o'clock, and didn't get off the piano until twelve. Then the people bought him a drink, and he kept playing, medley after medley. After the first set of about an hour,

I said, "When you gonna take an intermission?" He said, "We don't take intermission." He just looked at me like I was crazy. And by that time your tongue is hangin' out. This son-of-a-bitch was Hugh Wiley(?).
I had seen him ...(?)... But (?) Hugh Wiley(?) played for the Society people, too. There was about a half-a-dozen of them that played for the Society...
Yes. What's his name was the top one. Luckey was...
